title: He saw fire fall from heaven…
paragraphs: He saw fire fall from heaven…
…but his own heart was still cold.
He stood close enough to feel the heat, to hear the crack of burning sacrifice, to watch an entire nation fall on their faces and cry, “The Lord, He is God!”
Because it’s possible to witness power…
It’s possible to stand in holy moments…
That servant on Mount Carmel didn’t just see a miracle.
“How long will you go limping between two different opinions?” (1 Kings 18:21)
That question wasn’t just for Israel.
we’ve mastered looking close to God without fully surrendering to God.
There are rooms we haven’t opened.
but not to touch what we’re protecting.
So we stand like that servant.
And the silence of that condition is dangerous.
Because proximity to God is not the same as surrender to God.
He heard truth from the mouth of Christ Himself.
You can be around the presence…
God didn’t send fire just to impress people.
He sent fire to expose hearts.
“Then the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.”
He burns through the layers we try to hide behind.
Because that fire wasn’t just judgment.
But here’s where it gets personal.
that quiet observer in the background…
he represents something we don’t like to admit.
He represents the believer who has seen enough to know God is real—
but hasn’t surrendered enough to be transformed.
He represents the one who serves externally—
The one who helps build the altar—
Maybe you’ve even helped others encounter Him.
But when it comes to your hidden life—
Still a quiet “not yet” to full surrender.
And here’s the truth that cuts—
God is not impressed by how close you stand.
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”
Because fire doesn’t fall on pride.
But here’s where grace steps in—
Because in Mount Carmel, the fire fell on the sacrifice.
the fire of judgment fell on Jesus.
“But He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities… and by His wounds we are healed.”
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
the sacrifice was consumed so the people could live.
Jesus was consumed so you could be saved.
Because you can’t keep standing at a distance.
You can’t keep watching from the sidelines.
You can’t keep saying “I believe” while living like you don’t.
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.”
So here’s the question that won’t let you go—
Are you just watching fire fall?
Or are you willing to become the sacrifice?
To stop limping between two lives.
“Jesus, You can have all of me.”
Because the same God who sent fire on Carmel…
And He’s not asking for perfection.
What are you still holding back?
What part of your life is still untouched by God?
Because the altar is not a place of loss—
And if this stirred something deep in you…
